stories.label: North Korea fires missiles days after South Korea's hypersonic test
stories.summary: North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles toward the sea off its east coast at about 09:20 local time on Monday, South Korea's Joint Chiefs said, days after Seoul tested a hypersonic missile of its own. Lead with the launch as Seoul's military gives it (number, type, range, where they fell), attributed, and say what Tokyo and Washington reported. The mechanism: an action-reaction cycle in which each side's test is the other's justification; say what South Korea tested and when, what Pyongyang has said, and which UN resolutions bar the North's ballistic launches. One clause, only if a page has it: a Russian minister arrived in Pyongyang the same day. Sentiment differs little across outlets; write from Reuters and Al Jazeera, and use TASS and Mehr (Russian and Iranian state media) only where they agree. Dateline Seoul.

stories.label: US arrests fugitive in $2 billion Venezuelan bribery scheme
stories.summary: Alvaro Pulido Vargas, the Colombian businessman accused with Alex Saab of bribing Venezuelan officials and laundering money skimmed from the state's subsidised food programme, has been arrested and faces federal charges in Florida. Lead with the arrest and what is not known (when and where he was taken), then the charge: who is accused of paying whom, how much (the $2 billion figure, attributed to prosecutors), and through which contracts. The mechanism: food-import contracts for Venezuelans who could not afford to eat were overpriced and the difference moved through US banks, which is what gives a Florida court jurisdiction. Who it lands on: the Venezuelans the food boxes were meant for. Say what became of Saab's own case and what Caracas has said, only as the pages give it; state the allegations as allegations. Fox News frames it through Maduro; write from the NYT account. Dateline Miami. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: US judge orders halt to taxpayer-funded promo ads of Trump
stories.summary: A federal judge ruled on Sunday night that Donald Trump must cancel the remaining television ads promoting him that were paid for with millions in public money, granting an order sought by the watchdog Common Cause weeks before the midterm elections. Lead with the order: which court and judge, what it stops and from when, and how much was spent and by which department (the feed tags Homeland Security). The mechanism: say which law bars the use of appropriated funds for political promotion, what the government argued (Trump called the ads 'positive promotion for our great USA'), and whether the ruling is temporary and will be appealed. The accountability point: an incumbent using the state's advertising budget in an election season, stopped by a private group's lawsuit, not by Congress or an inspector. Single source. Dateline as the report places the court. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: FT: US threatens to halt arms supplies to Ukraine under PURL programme
stories.summary: New since yesterday's pieces on Zelenskiy's refinery offer and the Duma member doubting Trump's 'energy ceasefire' (one clause each): Washington has moved from demand to threat. The Financial Times and Axios report that the Trump administration is threatening to stop weapons deliveries under PURL, the scheme through which NATO allies pay for US-made arms for Ukraine, and to cut intelligence sharing, unless Kyiv stops striking Russian oil refineries. Lead with the threat and its terms, attributed to the FT and Axios as Ukrainska Pravda relays them; quote the White House official ('Trump is really mad') only with that attribution. The mechanism: the weapons are bought by Europeans, so the US is withholding goods others have paid for to protect fuel prices at home before the midterms; say what PURL has delivered and what Kyiv and European buyers have said. Name the series plainly: the price of Brent crude, which the refinery strikes and the truce claim both move. Who it lands on: Ukrainians under attack on their grid before winter. Write from Ukrainska Pravda (Ukrainian, independent) and Dawn; RT, TASS and TRT World are state media, used only where they quote Axios or the FT. The Bloomberg link in the cluster is a different story (EU curbs on Chinese inverters): do not use it. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Bipartisan group of US senators opposes Trump's Russian diesel deal
stories.summary: A bipartisan group of US senators has told Trump to 'immediately reverse course' on allowing imports of Russian diesel, saying the decision breaks federal law and hands Moscow revenue for its war. Lead with the letter: who signed it (name the Republicans), which statute they say was violated, and what they demand. The mechanism: say what the administration lifted and why (diesel prices at home before the midterms, with the Gulf war and Hormuz squeezing supply), how much Russian diesel is involved and what it earns Moscow, only with figures the pages give, and what Congress can actually do beyond a letter. The accountability point: sanctions written into law, set aside by the executive for a price at the pump, and challenged from inside the president's own party. Distinct from the separate piece this cycle on the threat to Ukraine's arms supply (one clause at most). Sentiment diverges: note where the BBC and Politico differ on the legal question. Dateline Washington. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: War and high debt to dominate IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok
stories.summary: Finance ministers and central bankers gather in Bangkok this week for the IMF and World Bank annual meetings under what the report calls the biggest energy supply shock on record, a widening Middle East war and rising interest rates. Lead with what the meetings open onto, in figures the page gives: growth forecasts, debt levels, and what the war has done to fuel costs. The mechanism: dear oil and diesel raise import bills and inflation, central banks raise rates, and governments that borrowed in dollars pay more to service debt just as revenue falls; say which countries the page names as most exposed and what the IMF and the Bank can offer them (lending, debt relief) against what they are asking for. Name the series plainly: the price of Brent crude and the Fed's interest rate. Who it lands on: importing countries of Asia and Africa, many of them Muslim-majority, that are party to none of the wars. This is a curtain-raiser: state no outcome and write only what is scheduled and said. Al Jazeera is the one source. Dateline Bangkok.

stories.label: Safety and immunogenicity of a BPL-inactivated, whole-virus, universal influenza vaccine: a randomized, double-blinded, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, phase 1 clinical trial
stories.summary: A candidate 'universal' flu vaccine, made from whole inactivated viruses and meant to protect across influenza strains instead of the few picked each season, has passed its first human trial, a randomised, placebo-controlled phase 1 study reported in Nature Communications. Lead with that in plain words and with what phase 1 does and does not show: safety and immune response, not protection. The mechanism for a technical reader: say why seasonal vaccines must be reformulated yearly (they target the fast-mutating head of haemagglutinin), what this candidate contains and why whole-virus, BPL-inactivated particles might raise broader immunity, how many volunteers there were, the doses and routes tested (the trial is double-dummy, so two routes were compared), the side effects and the breadth of the antibody and T-cell responses. Why it matters: a vaccine that need not be matched to each year's strain would matter most where annual campaigns do not reach, and in a pandemic. Name the authors, institutions and funder, and state the limits they give. Read the paper first and claim no more than it does. Single source. Dateline the city of the lead institution.

stories.label: Wildlife populations have declined 73% since 1970—but many of the world's animals still aren't being counted
stories.summary: The WWF's 2026 Living Planet Index puts the average decline in monitored wildlife populations at 73% since 1970, and the piece's point is what that number is not: it does not mean 73% of animals are gone, and many species and regions are not counted at all. Lead with the figure and its correct reading in one sentence each. The mechanism for a technical reader: say how the index is built (an average of proportional changes across monitored populations, so a small population halving weighs as much as a large one), which groups and regions are over- and under-represented in the data, and how the result shifts by region or habitat (freshwater, Latin America, Africa) as the page gives it. Why it matters: the headline number steers conservation money, and the gaps fall in the tropics, where most biodiversity and the least monitoring are. Name the authors of the analysis and state the limits they give. The feed entry is a teaser: read the page first and write only what it supports. Single source. Dateline the city of the lead author's institution.

stories.label: 累计43亿！国内最大AI Infra融资诞生，无问芯穹C轮拿下23亿
stories.summary: Infinigence AI (无问芯穹; confirm the English name from the page), a three-year-old Tsinghua spin-out, has closed a 2.3 billion yuan Series C, taking its total to 4.3 billion yuan, which Zhidx, a mainland Chinese tech outlet, calls the largest raise in China's AI-infrastructure sector; an IPO is reported to be in preparation. Lead with the round and what the company does, not the superlative. The mechanism for a technical reader: it owns no data centres and makes neither models nor chips; it sells the software layer that lets one model train and serve across mixed hardware, having run a 70-billion-parameter training job across four Chinese chips (Huawei Ascend, Iluvatar, MetaX, Moore Threads) and two foreign ones (AMD, Nvidia). Say why that is a necessity in China and not abroad: export controls left the country with a patchwork of accelerators, so the scheduling layer is where efficiency is won. Give the company's own performance and cost claims as claims. The structural point: state funds, Tencent, Baidu and Lenovo are all backing the same neutral layer. The piece is promotional in tone: translate figures exactly, attribute every judgement to Zhidx or the company, and leave out the valuation comparison with US firms unless stated as the outlet's view. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Shanghai or Beijing, as the piece places the company.

stories.label: 10亿！上海大模型创企拿下新融资
stories.summary: MOSI (模思智能), the Shanghai company spun out of Fudan professor Qiu Xipeng's OpenMOSS group, which released China's first open ChatGPT-style model in February 2023, announced on Monday a pre-A round of more than 1 billion yuan led by Huakong Fund with a line of state-backed Shanghai funds, its second raise this year. Lead with the round and who is paying. The mechanism for a technical reader: unlike Zhipu or DeepSeek, it is not chasing general chat or coding models but real-time speech, vision and multimodal interaction for glasses, cars and robots; describe the planned MOSS Live design (a front model that keeps perceiving and talking while a back model reasons and acts), the 20-plus open-source models released in half a year, and its 'AI for AI' loop in which generative models make training data and understanding models filter it. The structural point: municipal and national state capital is funding university labs into companies, and this one publishes its weights. Translate figures exactly, attribute judgements to Zhidx, and note as the piece does that commercial use is unproven. Distinct from this cycle's piece on Infinigence (no cross-reference needed). Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Shanghai.

stories.label: Meta Muse引爆的这场“代理人战争”，字节和腾讯都坐不住了
stories.summary: TMTPost, a mainland Chinese business outlet, reports that Meta's Muse has set off what its headline calls an 'agent war', and that ByteDance and Tencent are now moving in response. The feed carries only the headline and one line, so read the page first and lead with the concrete events: what Meta shipped and when, and what ByteDance and Tencent have each announced or are reported to be building, with dates and product names. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what kind of agent Muse is and where it runs (inside a social or messaging app with a billion-plus users, if the piece says so), and why that threatens companies whose business is the same kind of super-app, WeChat and Douyin. The structural point, if the piece makes it: the contest over agents is moving from the model makers to whoever owns the place people already spend their time, and China's two largest platforms read a US rival's launch as a threat at home. In Chinese; translate names and figures exactly and attribute every judgement to TMTPost. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Beijing or Shenzhen, as the piece gives it.

stories.label: Iran says US response to its proposal to reopen Hormuz was 'insufficient'
stories.summary: New since the 10-10 piece on Putin relaying Tehran's terms to Trump (one clause): Washington has now answered, and Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei calls the reply to Iran's seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz 'insufficient', adding that if the conditions are not met the strait will not be opened to the Americans. Lead with the rejection, quoted exactly and attributed to Rezaei via Iranian state media as Reuters gives it. The mechanism: list the seven conditions as the pages give them, say through whom the proposal travelled (the UN General Assembly, Qatar), what the US offered back, and what remains of the US blockade of Iranian ports. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of Brent crude, both hostage to this exchange. Who it lands on: the crews in the strait (the IRGC claimed a second mine strike on a supertanker the same day, one clause) and Asian importers. The National and The New Arab are the regional outlets. Dateline Dubai or Tehran, as the reports give it.

stories.label: 'To keep oil prices from rising' -- Russian lawmaker questions Trump's energy ceasefire claim
stories.summary: New since this afternoon's piece on Zelenskiy offering to stop hitting Russian refineries if Moscow halts its attacks on Ukraine's energy system (one clause): Donald Trump announced on Sunday an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, and a senior member of the State Duma's energy committee says he has no information about any such deal and suggests Trump said it 'to keep oil prices from rising'. Lead with the gap: a ceasefire announced by a third party that one of the two sides says it knows nothing of. Quote Trump's announcement and the lawmaker exactly, name him and his post, and say what Kyiv and the Kremlin have each confirmed or not, only as the page gives it. The mechanism: Washington has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel and wants Russian refineries running and fuel cheap before the midterms, so an announcement alone can move the price of Brent crude; say what an energy truce would cover (refineries on one side, the power grid on the other) and whether strikes continued on Sunday. Who it lands on: Ukrainians facing winter on a damaged grid. The Kyiv Independent is a Ukrainian outlet and the one source; a Duma member is not the Kremlin, so do not present his remark as Moscow's position. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Everyone wants SCOTUS to take up prediction markets: State of Crypto
stories.summary: A run of amicus briefs filed last week urges the US Supreme Court to decide whether sports-based prediction-market contracts are 'swaps', and on Friday the CFTC published two proposals of its own on the question, one already in effect. Lead with the legal question and what turns on it, not the newsletter form: if the contracts are swaps, a federal derivatives regulator governs them and state gambling law does not; if they are not, each state can ban or tax them as betting. The mechanism: say which case the court is asked to take, which lower courts split and how, who filed the briefs (exchanges such as Kalshi and Polymarket, states, tribes, leagues, as the page names them) and what each of the CFTC's two proposals does. The accountability point: an industry that grew by offering sports bets under a commodities licence now wants the court to ratify it, while the regulator writes the rule in its favour before the court speaks; state that only as far as the piece supports it. Distinct from the earlier piece on the Clarity Act's failure (one clause at most). CoinDesk is a trade outlet: no price commentary. Single source. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Authorities impose Section 144 in Karachi, ban gatherings of more than 5 people till Oct 20
stories.summary: New since today's pieces on the emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the sealed roads around Peshawar and Lahore, and the advisory council (one clause): the ban on assembly has now reached Pakistan's largest city, in a province the emergency does not cover. The Karachi commissioner has imposed Section 144, prohibiting gatherings of more than five people until 20 October, citing protests that 'inconvenience the public' and a 'deterioration of the law and order situation'. Lead with the order, its dates exactly as the notification gives them (the feed's headline and first line differ, so take them from the page), and who issued it. The mechanism for a reader outside Pakistan: Section 144 of the colonial-era Code of Criminal Procedure lets an administrator, not a court, ban assembly by notification; say what it prohibits, the penalty, and which protest or march it is aimed at, only as Dawn gives it. The structural point: Rawalpindi on 10-10, Peshawar and Lahore on 10-11, now Karachi in PPP-run Sindh, so the restriction on gathering now covers the country's main cities without any nationwide declaration. Say what PTI or other parties have announced in response if the page has it. Dawn is the Pakistani outlet and the only source. Dateline Karachi.

stories.label: Checks, cops in plainclothes at all gates: Dhruv Rathee's society wakes up to unfamiliar sight
stories.summary: New since today's pieces on the Delhi detentions, the release of the Cockroach Janata Party leaders and the chief justice declining to meet the opposition (one clause): the policing has moved from the protest site to a critic's home. Residents and workers at Kendriya Vihar in Gurgaon's Sector 56 say about 50 plainclothes personnel entered the housing society late on 9 October, its three gates were shut through the night and police gathered around the home of Dhruv Rathee, a YouTuber with one of the largest political audiences in India. Lead with what the residents describe, attributed to them, and say what the police give as the reason and legal basis, whether Rathee was detained, restricted or served any order, and what he has said, only as the page gives it. The mechanism: preventive policing of a person who has not been charged, carried out by a neighbouring state's force ahead of a protest in the capital over the voter-roll revision and the demand that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar go. For scale, Drop Site News reports the election commission removed more than 130 million people from the rolls (attribute the figure to Drop Site). The Times of India is the one source on the Gurgaon scene. Write your own headline. Dateline Gurgaon.

stories.label: Death toll from Israeli attacks on Lebanon nears 4,390 -- health ministry
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry says at least one civilian was killed in the south on Sunday as Israeli troops continue operations against Hezbollah, bringing the death toll in Lebanon since the escalation began on 2 March to nearly 4,390. Lead with the dead: Sunday's victim, where and how as the ministry gives it, then the cumulative toll and the wounded, each attributed to the ministry and quoted from its statement. TASS is Russian state media and the only source in the feed, but it is relaying the Lebanese ministry: attribute to both ('the health ministry said, according to Russian state news agency TASS') and state nothing TASS adds of its own. The mechanism: say where Israeli forces are operating inside Lebanon, what Israel says of the day's strikes if the page has it, and how many of the dead the ministry counts as women, children and medics if it breaks them down. Dignity runs both ways: give Israeli dead from the same front in a clause if the page does. The structural point: seven months of a war that kills daily and now draws almost no coverage beside Hormuz and Riyadh. This is a short live-file entry: write only what it supports. No Lebanese or regional outlet in the feed carries it. Dateline Beirut.

stories.label: Iran ready to help start dialogue btw S. Arabia, Yemen: FM
stories.summary: New since today's pieces on the second attack on Riyadh's airport and the joint demand by Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Pakistan and Türkiye that the Houthis stop (one clause): Iran's foreign minister phoned his Saudi counterpart, Faisal bin Farhan, on Sunday night, said there is no military solution and offered Tehran's help in starting a dialogue between Riyadh and Sanaa. Lead with the call and the offer, quoted exactly. Mehr is Iranian state media and the only source: attribute everything to it ('Iran's state-run Mehr news agency reported'), and say plainly that the feed carries no Saudi account of the call or reply to the offer. The mechanism: Iran arms and backs the Houthis, so the offer comes from the patron of the party firing on Saudi airports, while Iran itself is at war with the US and bargaining over Hormuz; say what the minister said about the airport attacks and their dead, if anything, and what Riyadh's stated position on talks with Sanaa has been. The structural point: Tehran is positioning itself as the channel to the Houthis at the moment four Sunni-majority states lined up against them. This is a short live-file entry: write only what it supports. Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: 'Who can we trust?' Prosecutors say little has changed since Tracy Brown was killed
stories.summary: South African prosecutors say they are no safer inside or outside courthouses than they were when their colleague Tracy Brown, a Nelson Mandela Bay prosecutor, was shot dead in a contract killing; the men accused of ordering it are still awaiting a trial date. Lead with the prosecutors' own account, quoted exactly, against what the Department of Justice and the police say they have done. The mechanism: say who Brown was and what cases she handled, who is accused of ordering the hit and why (as the charge sheet has it, not as fact), what protection a prosecutor is entitled to and what they actually get (escorts, secure parking, court security), and how many court officials have been attacked or killed, with the source of each figure. The accountability point: a state that cannot protect the people who prosecute organised crime loses the cases along with them, and the officials saying so do not trust the police assigned to guard them. Name the dead as the report names them. Daily Maverick is the South African outlet and the only source. Dateline Gqeberha.

stories.label: Quantum 'birthmarks' hold lasting traces of a system's past
stories.summary: Physicists report that some quantum systems keep a permanent trace of how they started, a 'birthmark', instead of forgetting it as a well-mixed system should. Lead with that in plain words. The mechanism for a technical reader: a classical chaotic system is ergodic, meaning that over time it visits its available configurations so thoroughly that its long-run behaviour no longer reveals its starting point; say what the researchers found a quantum system does instead, how large and how lasting the effect is, whether this is theory, simulation or experiment and on what system, and how it relates to known exceptions such as quantum scars. Why it matters: thermalisation is the assumption under statistical mechanics, and memory of the initial state bears on how quantum devices hold or lose information. Name the authors, institutions and journal, and state the limits the authors give. The feed entry is a teaser: read the page first, write only what it supports and claim no more than the paper does. Single source. Dateline the city of the lead institution.

stories.label: Türkiye 'strongly' condemns deadly Houthi militia attack on Riyadh airport
stories.summary: New since the 10-10 piece on the missile that hit Riyadh's airport and this morning's piece on the Houthis declaring Saudi airports targets (one clause each): King Khalid International Airport was attacked a second time on Sunday, the Saudi civil aviation authority now puts the toll of the first strike at 12 killed and 309 wounded, and Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Pakistan and Türkiye jointly demanded an immediate halt to Houthi attacks. Lead with the dead and wounded, attributed to the Saudi authority (GACA), and the second attack with its casualties as GACA gives them, not with Ankara's condemnation; say who the victims were (travellers, airport workers, their nationalities) if a page does. The mechanism: four of the largest Sunni-majority states are lining up publicly against the Houthis while the group closes a country's airspace by missile and announcement; say what the joint statement commits them to beyond words, what the Houthis say they are answering, and whether the airport is operating. Write from The National and Al Arabiya (Gulf outlets) for the toll and the joint demand; TRT World is Turkish state media, used for Ankara's statement, and TASS (https://tass.com/emergencies/2200577) relays the GACA statement on the second attack. Write your own headline. Dateline Riyadh.

stories.label: 72 killed in airstrike on gold mine on Sudan-Egypt border
stories.summary: The Sudanese rights group Emergency Lawyers says an air strike on Saturday killed 72 workers at a gold mine on the Sudan-Egypt border, and accuses Egypt's air force of carrying it out. Lead with the 72 dead and who they were (mine workers), then the accusation, stated as the group's claim and quoted exactly: no government, army or independent confirmation is in the feed, so say that plainly, and give Cairo's and Khartoum's responses only if the page has them. The mechanism: say where the mine is and who controls the area, why artisanal gold on that border matters (it finances the war's armed parties and is smuggled north), and what Egypt's role in Sudan's war has been, only as the page gives it. The accountability point: a state outside the war is accused of killing civilians at work on a neighbour's territory, and the only body counting the dead is a volunteer lawyers' group. This is a short live-file entry: write only what it supports. Middle East Eye is the one source; the feed carries no Sudanese or Egyptian outlet on this. Write your own headline. Dateline as the report places the mine, or Khartoum.

stories.label: Poland arrests man over plot to kill PM Donald Tusk
stories.summary: New since this morning's piece on the three school attacks, which ended on police receiving information about a possible attack (one clause): Poland has detained a man accused of plotting to assassinate Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, and Tusk confirmed the arrest himself. Lead with the arrest: who was detained (age, nationality and background only as officials give them), where, by which service, and on what charge. The mechanism: say what Interior Minister Tomasz Siemoniak and the security services say the plot consisted of, how they learned of it, whether they allege a foreign hand or a link to the week's school violence, and state no link or motive the pages do not; say what protection and legal steps follow. The structural point: a NATO front-line government whose head and defence chief are targeted in the same week that copycat violence spread through its schools. Sentiment diverges between outlets, so note where the BBC, Deutsche Welle and Al Jazeera differ on what is established. TRT World is Turkish state media, used where the others agree. Write your own headline. Dateline Warsaw.

stories.label: CJI Surya Kant declines Rahul Gandhi meet over vote chori plea
stories.summary: New since this morning's pieces on the Delhi detentions continuing despite a Supreme Court order (one clause): Chief Justice Surya Kant has declined the opposition INDIA bloc's request to meet him on Monday over the voter-roll revision (SIR) and its 'vote chori' (vote theft) allegation, saying the matter is before the court, which closes the route the opposition had chosen and leaves its march in Delhi as the next step. Lead with the refusal and his stated reasons, quoted exactly. The mechanism for a reader outside India: say what the opposition asked for and why it went to the chief justice in person (Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge want Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar removed), why a judge hearing a case cannot meet one side, where the SIR petitions stand, and what the opposition says it will do on Monday. Then the scale: Drop Site News (https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/india-delhi-protests-voter-purge), an investigative outlet, reports that the election commission removed more than 130 million people from the rolls and describes the force used against demonstrators; give that figure attributed to Drop Site, and say who was removed if it documents it. The structural point: the dispute over who may vote now has no venue but the street and a court that will not be hurried. All three cluster sources are Indian outlets. Write your own headline. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Who are the members of the newly formed KP Advisory Council?
stories.summary: New since today's pieces on the emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the sealed roads around Peshawar (one clause): the federal government has named an 11-member technocratic KP Advisory Council to help Governor Faisal Karim Kundi run the province in place of the dismissed elected cabinet. Lead with the decision, not the roster: a province of roughly 40 million is now administered by a federally appointed governor and eleven unelected advisers. The mechanism: say who sits on the council and where they come from (retired bureaucrats, police, revenue officials, as Dawn lists them), which portfolios they take, what legal standing an advisory council has under governor's rule and to whom it answers, and how long the arrangement can last before parliament must act. Say whether anyone on it has ties to the parties in the federal coalition or to the military, only as Dawn records it, and what PTI has said of it. The structural point: emergency rule has moved from suspending a government to building its replacement. Dawn is the Pakistani outlet and the only source. Write your own headline. Dateline Peshawar, or Islamabad if the notification is reported from there.

stories.label: Pentagon raises official US death toll in Iran war -- RT World News
stories.summary: The Pentagon has raised its official count of US military deaths in the war with Iran from 18 to 21, revising a tally in its Defense Casualty Analysis System that had been under-reported, Russian state broadcaster RT reports, citing the Washington Post. Lead with the revision and the two numbers, attributed: RT is state media of a government hostile to Washington and the only source in the feed, so state as fact only what it attributes to the Pentagon's own database or to the Post, and name both. The mechanism: say which deaths were added, where and when they occurred (the feed tags Kuwait and the US Navy), whether they are classed as hostile or non-hostile, and how the omission came to light. The accountability point: a government at war controls the count of its own dead, and the count moved only after a newspaper checked it. Dignity cuts both ways: in a clause, give the Iranian and regional death tolls of the same war if the page does, with attribution. Say nothing RT adds as commentary. Write your own headline. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Yemen government says forces advancing toward Bab al-Mandeb, carried out strikes on Houthis in Taiz
stories.summary: New since the 10-10 piece on the Yemeni government's advance around Bab al-Mandeb (one clause): the Saudi-backed government now says its forces have taken Dhubab and the positions around it and cut the road between Dhubab and Mocha, and that it carried out strikes on Houthi forces in Taiz; lead with those specific claims, attributed to the prime minister's office and quoted exactly, and say that they come from one party to the war with no independent confirmation in the feed. The mechanism: Dhubab sits on the coast just north of the strait, so say what holding it and the Mocha road gives a force over the eastern shore of the passage, and what the Houthis say in reply if the page has it. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the gate to the Red Sea and Suez, which this ground fight now runs alongside. Who it lands on: the civilians of the Taiz coast, and the crews and importers who depend on the strait while Hormuz is also under fire. One clause: the Houthis are striking Riyadh's airport the same weekend. This is a short live-file entry: write only what it supports. Middle East Eye is the one source; no Yemeni outlet is in the feed. Write your own headline. Dateline Aden, or as the report gives it.

stories.label: Crypto executives see upside in Clarity's failure, but legal experts warn uncertainty will persist
stories.summary: The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, the bill meant to settle which US regulator governs crypto markets, has failed to advance in the Senate, so the rules will now be written by the SEC and the CFTC through rule-making and enforcement instead of by statute. Lead with the failure and what it changes, not with the executives' optimism: when the bill stalled and on what, as the page gives it. The mechanism: say what the act would have done (split jurisdiction between the two agencies, defined when a token is a security or a commodity), what agency rules can and cannot do without it (they can be reversed by the next administration or struck down in court), and why CoinDesk's sources think that favours decentralised-finance projects in the short run while established exchanges keep their advantage. The accountability point: an industry that spent heavily to get a law is now content with regulators its allies appoint; state that only as far as the piece supports it, and attribute each judgement to the executive or lawyer who makes it. CoinDesk is a trade outlet: give no price commentary. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Washington. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: New study shows effects of hypoxia in Florida's Banana River
stories.summary: Low oxygen in the water of Florida's Banana River lagoon is causing nutrients buried in the bottom sediment to be released again, feeding the harmful algal blooms that deplete the oxygen in the first place, a study led by Austin Fox of Florida Tech finds from the most widespread oxygen survey yet made of the river. Lead with that loop in plain words. The mechanism for a technical reader: say which nutrients are released and why oxygen-poor sediment gives them up (the chemistry of phosphorus and nitrogen at the sediment surface, as the page explains it), how and where oxygen was measured, how much of the river was hypoxic and when, and how the internal release compares with what flows in from land. Why it matters beyond Florida: a water body can go on feeding its own blooms after pollution from outside is cut, which changes what a clean-up has to do, and the same process works in enclosed lagoons and estuaries elsewhere. Name the journal and state the limits (one lagoon, the period sampled). The feed entry is a teaser from a university release: write only what the page supports and claim no more than the authors do. Single source. Dateline Melbourne, Florida. US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: At least 109 dead, over 100 missing as migrant boat capsizes off Djibouti
stories.summary: At least 109 migrants, 15 of them children, are dead and more than 100 missing after a boat carrying 350 people from Djibouti to Yemen capsized near Obock, the IOM says. Lead with the dead and the missing, each figure attributed to the IOM, and say who they were (mostly Ethiopians, if the pages say so) and how many were rescued. The mechanism: this is the 'eastern route' from the Horn of Africa across the Bab el-Mandeb strait to Yemen and on to Saudi Arabia, run by smugglers who overload boats; say what caused the capsizing only as the IOM or survivors give it, how many have died on the route this year, and why people still cross into a country at war. The structural point: one of the world's deadliest migration routes runs through a strait now contested by warships, and its dead draw a fraction of the attention given to the Mediterranean. Write from Reuters, the BBC and Al Jazeera (the regional outlet in the cluster). Write your own headline. Dateline Obock, or Djibouti if the reports file from there.

stories.label: Timeline: A concise history of emergency rule in Pakistan
stories.summary: New since this morning's piece on the emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (one clause): the order is now being enforced on the ground and beyond the province. Shipping containers have been placed to block roads around Peshawar, and in Lahore the administration sealed all general bus terminals overnight and intercity services were suspended, stranding passengers (the two Dawn news items in the sources). Lead with the sealed roads and terminals, not the timeline: where, on whose order, and what march or gathering they are meant to stop, as Dawn gives it. The mechanism: the emergency and governor's rule were approved under Articles 232 and 234 of the constitution; say what each article permits, what parliament must do and by when, and use the Dawn timeline for one fact of history: every province has been placed under emergency or governor's rule at some point, so say when KP last was. Say what PTI and the dismissed provincial government have announced, and whether any court has been petitioned, only as the pages give it. Who it lands on: travellers and traders in two provinces whose movement is stopped by administrative order. Dawn is the Pakistani outlet the earlier piece lacked; Al Jazeera is the second source. Write your own headline. Dateline Peshawar.

stories.label: Homes and bridges swept away as fresh floods hit Nepal
stories.summary: A landslide-triggered flash flood on the Budhi Gandaki River in Nepal's Gorkha district has swept away houses and bridges and damaged part of a hydropower station; the army says about 50 people were rescued and no casualties are reported so far, and authorities ordered a mass evacuation downstream. Lead with what was destroyed and who was moved, each figure attributed, and say plainly that the toll may change. The mechanism: say what set it off as officials give it (a landslide damming or falling into the river, as the Hindustan Times headline has it), why Himalayan valleys flood in a surge with little warning, what 'fresh' refers to (earlier floods this season, with their toll if the pages give it), and which hydropower plant was hit and what it supplies. The structural point: Nepal builds its power supply and its settlements along the same steep rivers, so one slope failure takes out homes, roads and electricity together. This is a disaster report, filed under politics: say nothing about climate attribution unless a page does. Write your own headline. Dateline Gorkha, or Kathmandu if the reports file from there.

stories.label: Pope Leo XIV to undergo surgery to remove lump on lung
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV, 71, announced on Sunday that he will have surgery in the coming days to remove a nodular lesion on his lung, found early and described as 'circumscribed', the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate. Lead with his own announcement, quoted exactly, and what is and is not known: where and when the operation will be, whether a diagnosis has been given, and that the Vatican has not said the nodule is malignant unless a page reports it. The mechanism: say who governs the Church while a pope is under anaesthesia or recovering (there is no deputy; routine business continues under the Secretary of State, and nothing in canon law covers an incapacitated pope), and what the Vatican says about his schedule. Why it matters beyond the Church: one clause on the 10-10 piece, in which the first US-born pope called the death penalty 'inadmissible' as Washington weighs a livestreamed execution, a voice now off the stage for a time. Report no prognosis and no speculation on succession. Write from the AP copy and Deutsche Welle. Write your own headline. Dateline Vatican City; not a US dateline.

stories.label: Ukraine will stop hitting refineries if Russia halts energy attacks, Zelenskiy says
stories.summary: New since the 10-10 pieces on Trump saying Ukraine should 'get a new president' and on Kallas and the diesel sanctions (one clause each): Trump on Saturday demanded that Kyiv unilaterally stop striking Russian oil refineries, and Volodymyr Zelenskiy answered on Sunday with a counter-offer: Ukraine will halt those strikes if Moscow stops attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Lead with the offer and the demand it answers, both quoted exactly. The mechanism: Ukraine's drones on refineries are its one means of cutting the fuel revenue that funds the war, and Washington has just lifted sanctions on Russian diesel to lower prices at home, so a US president now has a direct interest in Russian refineries running; say how much refining capacity the strikes have taken out and what Russia's strikes have done to Ukraine's grid before winter, only with figures the page gives. Say whether Moscow has replied. Who it lands on: Ukrainians facing winter without power, and whoever pays for diesel. Do not name a crude price series unless the page gives a figure. Reuters is the source; the Yahoo item is the same copy. Write your own headline. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Manus恢复“单身”身价再涨，但战场已“大变天”
stories.summary: TMTPost, a mainland Chinese business outlet, reports that the AI-agent company Manus has taken in US$500 million of new funding and seen its valuation jump again, now that it is, in the headline's word, 'single' again, while the market for agents it helped start has changed around it. The feed carries only the headline and one line, so read the page first and lead with the concrete event: who put in the $500 million, at what valuation, and what 'single again' refers to (a tie-up or acquisition that ended; state it only as the piece documents it, with who ended it and why). The mechanism for a technical reader: say what Manus sells (a general agent built on other labs' models), why that position is harder now that the model makers ship their own agents, and what the outlet thinks the money buys. The structural point: a Chinese-founded AI company caught between Washington's and Beijing's rules on who may own it, if the piece makes that case. In Chinese; translate figures exactly and attribute every judgement to TMTPost. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline as the piece places the company (Singapore or Beijing).

stories.label: 本末科技，还没吃上具身智能这碗饭
stories.summary: TMTPost, a mainland Chinese business outlet, examines Benmo Technology (本末科技, which trades in English as DirectDrive Tech; confirm the name from the page), a robotics-component maker presented as an 'embodied intelligence' company whose embodied-intelligence business brings in just 5% of revenue. The feed carries only the headline and that figure, so read the page first and lead with the gap: what the company says it is against where its money comes from. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what it actually makes and sells (direct-drive motors and actuators, and to whom), its revenue, profit or loss and the source of the figures (a listing prospectus, if that is the occasion), and why joints and motors are where much of a humanoid robot's cost sits. The structural point: China's robot boom is being financed on the embodied-AI label, and the filings show how little of the revenue is yet robots. In Chinese; translate figures exactly, attribute judgements to TMTPost, and state as fact only what the filing or the piece documents. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline the company's home city as the piece gives it.

stories.label: CJP activists to be produced before magistrate; court dismisses plea
stories.summary: New since the 10-10 pieces on the Delhi detentions (one clause): the detained Cockroach Janata Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two colleagues, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, are to be produced on Sunday before an executive magistrate at Delhi Cantt police station, and a Saket court has dismissed the plea by the party's legal head, Ratna Singh, for a police case against officers over her alleged restraint. Lead with the two decisions: who is being produced, before whom and on what grounds, and what the court said in refusing the plea. The mechanism for a reader outside India: an executive magistrate is an officer of the administration, not a judge, and preventive detention is reviewed by that officer, so the same executive that ordered the detentions hears them first; say which provision the police cite and how long it allows them to hold someone. Then the street: Jantar Mantar stays barricaded for a second day with 30 traffic points restricted, from the Hindustan Times. Say whether the opposition leaders detained on Saturday were released, and where the Supreme Court matter stands, only as the pages give it. Detention figures as attributed. Write your own headline. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Pakistan Imposes Emergency in Stronghold of Imran Khan's Party
stories.summary: President Asif Ali Zardari has declared a state of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and suspended its elected provincial government, the one province run by Imran Khan's PTI, after weeks of confrontation between the party and Shehbaz Sharif's federal government. Lead with the order: what it suspends, under which article of the constitution, who now runs the province (the governor, a federal appointee) and for how long. The mechanism for a reader outside Pakistan: say what the constitution requires for such an emergency (parliamentary approval and its deadline), what the centre cites as the ground, what PTI was protesting for, and what courts can review. New since the 10-10 piece on the Section 144 assembly ban in Rawalpindi (one clause): the ban on gatherings in the garrison city was followed within a day by the removal of the opposition's only government. Who it lands on: the province's roughly 40 million people, governed by an administration they did not elect, in the region that bears most of the country's militant violence. Say what PTI and the dismissed chief minister said and whether they will go to court or the street, only as the pages give it. Write from Reuters; the Economic Times is an Indian outlet and Bloomberg may not fetch. The feed carries no Pakistani outlet on this event. Write your own headline. Dateline Islamabad, or Peshawar if the reports file from there.

stories.label: Detentions continue in Delhi despite SC order, 100 held from CP
stories.summary: New since this morning's piece on the Cockroach Janata Party founders being produced before an executive magistrate (one clause): India's Supreme Court has ordered that peaceful, unarmed protesters cannot be detained, the three leaders, Abhijeet Dipke among them, were released on Sunday and vowed new protests, and Delhi Police nonetheless detained about 100 more people around Connaught Place, including CPI(M) MP John Brittas. Lead with that gap: a court order and, the same day, detentions that continue. The mechanism: quote what the court ordered and on whose petition, say what legal basis the police give for Sunday's detentions and whether those held were released, and what the protest is about (the revision of voter lists and the demand that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign). Then the outside pressure: UN human rights chief Volker Türk criticised the detentions and India's foreign ministry called it 'unwarranted interference' (NDTV: https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/unwarranted-interference-india-slams-uns-remarks-on-delhi-detentions-12167716 ). The release and the leaders' statements are in the AP copy (https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2026-10-11/indias-cockroach-protest-movement-leaders-freed-from-detention ); the Deutsche Welle link is a live file. The structural point: the executive is testing how far it can go on holding people the country's highest court has said it may not hold. Detention figures as attributed. Write your own headline. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: Prime Minister Tusk addresses online 'glorification of violence' after Polish school attacks
stories.summary: Three attacks on schools in Poland's Mazovian province in four days, the third a stabbing that injured three, have led Prime Minister Donald Tusk to say on Sunday that they were 'spontaneous acts' driven by the online 'glorification of violence'. Lead with the three attacks: where, when, how many hurt or killed in each and who the attackers were (ages, pupils or not), as the AP copy gives it, then Tusk's words quoted exactly. The mechanism: say what investigators have found linking or not linking the attacks, which online spaces or content Tusk and the police point to, and what the government proposes (platform rules, school security), only as announced. Then the escalation: the Interior Ministry said on Sunday that police received information about a possible attack on Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz (Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/poland-says-police-got-information-about-possible-attack-pm-defence-minister-2026-10-11/ ); report it as the ministry states it and draw no link the pages do not. The structural point: copycat violence spreading through a country with almost no history of school attacks, and a government whose first answer is to regulate what is online. State no motive the police have not given, and do not name minors. Write your own headline. Dateline Warsaw.

stories.label: Isaias: East sees chance of flooding, winds, and tornadoes
stories.summary: Hurricane Isaias made landfall on the Florida Panhandle on Friday night at Category 2 strength; at least four people are dead and hundreds of thousands are without power across Florida and Alabama, and the storm, now inland, still threatens flooding and tornadoes across the US South and East through Sunday. Lead with the dead and the scale of the outages, each figure attributed (the Hindustan Times and BBC pages carry the toll), then where the storm is now and what is forecast. The mechanism: say where it came ashore and with what wind speed and surge, why the inland phase kills (rain and river flooding, tornadoes in the outer bands), which areas were ordered to evacuate, and what state and federal agencies have done. Name the dead as the reports name them. This is a disaster report, not a science piece: say nothing about climate attribution unless a page does. Do not write a forecast that will be stale in hours: give the forecast as of Sunday morning, attributed to the National Hurricane Center. TRT World is Turkish state media, used where the others agree. Write your own headline. Dateline Panama City or Pensacola, as the reports place the landfall. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: Houthis urge Saudi Arabia to cancel flights, declaring country's airports as their targets
stories.summary: New since the 10-10 piece on the missile that hit Terminal 3 of Riyadh's airport (one clause): the Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Saree, has declared all of Saudi Arabia's airports targets and again told airlines to cancel flights, and the warning is already moving traffic: Cochin International Airport says several flights between Kerala and Saudi Arabia and other Gulf destinations were cancelled on Sunday (Hindustan Times, independent, citing airport officials). Lead with the cancellations as the airport states them (which airlines and routes), then the threat that caused them, attributed to Saree and quoted exactly. The mechanism: an armed group with ballistic missiles is closing a country's airspace by announcement, because airlines and their insurers act on the warning before any missile is fired; say what Saudi authorities and carriers have said and which Saudi airports are operating, only as the pages give it. Who it lands on: the millions of South Asian workers in the kingdom, Kerala's above all, whose way home and whose remittances run through these routes, and pilgrims bound for Jeddah and Medina if a page mentions them. TASS is Russian state media relaying the Houthi statement from Doha: attribute it as such; the Hindustan Times item is the independent source. The feed carries no Saudi or Gulf outlet on this. Write your own headline. Dateline Riyadh, or Kochi if the cancellations lead.

stories.label: 李嘉诚1100亿港元套现电网，268亿逆势囤油砂，到底在赌什么
stories.summary: TMTPost, a mainland Chinese business outlet, examines why Li Ka-shing's group is cashing out of a British electricity network for HK$110 billion while putting 26.8 billion into Canadian oil sands, a move against the direction most large investors have taken on fossil fuels. Lead with the two transactions and their figures exactly as the piece gives them: which CK group companies, which assets, the buyers and sellers, the currency of the 26.8 billion, and the dates. The mechanism: say what a regulated grid earns (a return set by the UK regulator) against what oil sands earn with crude above $100 a barrel during the Gulf war, why oil sands are long-lived, high-cost reserves that pay when prices stay high, and what the outlet thinks Li is betting on. The structural point: Hong Kong's most-watched investor is moving capital out of regulated British infrastructure and into North American hydrocarbons, a read on both UK political risk and how long he expects expensive oil to last. Name the price of Brent crude only if the piece gives a figure. This is an analysis piece in Chinese, not a wire report: translate figures exactly, attribute every judgement to TMTPost, and state as fact only the transactions it documents. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Hong Kong.

stories.label: Massive LPG tanker targeted in Hormuz: IRGC
stories.summary: New since the 10-09 piece on the Guards' claimed strike on a gas tanker and this morning's piece on Kpler's export figures (one clause each): Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps says a mine struck a crude oil supertanker in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, setting off a 'massive explosion', and accuses the vessel of taking an 'unauthorised' route, which is the first time the Iran-Oman 'safe route' has been enforced with a mine rather than a missile. Lead with the IRGC's statement as a claim by a party to the war: which ship, whose flag and cargo, casualties and spill only if the pages give them, and say that no shipowner, navy or independent confirmation is in the feed. The mechanism: a declared corridor plus mines outside it turns a strait into a toll gate that Tehran controls, and insurers, not navies, decide whether tankers sail. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of Brent crude. Who it lands on: the crew, and the Asian importers paying above $100 a barrel. The feed title and the Mehr and TASS items may describe the earlier LPG tanker strike: write the new event from the Middle East Eye update (a live-file entry, short) and The New Arab, and use Mehr and TASS, both state media, only for the IRGC's own words. Write your own headline. Dateline Dubai, or as the reports give it.

stories.label: US hits commercial tanker in Gulf of Oman as tensions flare
stories.summary: The US military says it struck and disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman that tried to run its naval blockade of Iranian ports, its first attack near Iran in more than a month. New since the 10-10 pieces on the IRGC's mine claim and Kpler's export figures (one clause each): both sides are now hitting merchant ships on the same weekend, and UKMTO separately reports an outbound tanker hit on the port side by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, with a fire aboard, the crew safe and ships asked to move from UAE anchorages (the Middle East Eye update, short; attribute to UKMTO and assign it to no one). Lead with the US strike as CENTCOM states it: which ship, flag, cargo and crew, casualties only as the pages give them, and what the owner or Tehran says. The FT also reports 12 killed and 300 injured in a missile strike: give it as the page does, with place and attribution. The mechanism: a blockade enforced by fire on one side and a mined 'safe route' on the other leaves insurers and crews, not navies, deciding whether cargo moves. Name the series plainly: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and the price of Brent crude. Who it lands on: the seafarers, and Asian importers paying above $100 a barrel. Al Jazeera and Middle East Eye are the regional outlets. Write your own headline. Dateline Muscat or Dubai, as the reports give it; not a US dateline.

stories.label: Kallas: EU won't ease pressure on Russia
stories.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Saturday that Washington's lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel hands Moscow revenue to fight its war, and Euromaidan Press reports the EU plans to pass its largest sanctions package yet within two days. New since the 10-09 pieces on the Trump-Putin diesel accord and Russia's 300,000-tonne offer (one clause each): the allies' sanctions regimes are now moving in opposite directions, and there is a date on Europe's answer. Lead with the split and the package: what it targets and when it is to be adopted, only as the pages give it, and which member states could block it. The mechanism: say what the US eased and why (fuel prices before the midterms, as Arab News' AFP copy puts it), how much diesel revenue is at stake if a page gives a figure, and why sanctions that one large buyer abandons lose force for everyone still enforcing them. Who it lands on: Ukrainians under the strikes that revenue pays for, and European consumers who keep paying more for diesel than Americans will. This is about sanctions and the diesel trade, not a crude price recap. Euromaidan Press is a Ukrainian advocacy-leaning outlet: use it for the package's timing, attributed, and Arab News for Kallas's words. Write your own headline. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: EXPLAINER: Tinubu's petrol relief plan, Atiku's subsidy proposal -- how they differ, who pays
stories.summary: Nigeria's government has extended a petrol discount at state-owned NNPC's filling stations and proposed measures to stabilise pump prices, while opposition figure Atiku Abubakar proposes supporting domestic refineries instead. Lead with the news, not the explainer form: the extension, the size of the discount and the pump price in naira, and for how long, as Premium Times gives them. The mechanism: Tinubu removed the fuel subsidy in 2023, so say what this discount is if not a subsidy, who funds it (NNPC's books, the federation account, the states), how Atiku's plan would route the money through refiners such as Dangote instead, and what each costs. The structural point: Africa's largest oil producer is rationing relief from an oil price driven above $100 by a war in the Gulf, four months before the 2027 elections, and the bill lands on the same public accounts either way. Who it lands on: Nigerians whose transport and food costs follow the pump price. Do not name a currency or crude series unless the page gives the figure. Premium Times is the regional outlet and the only source. Write your own headline. Dateline Abuja.

stories.label: South Korean container ship ends voyage along Northern Sea Route
stories.summary: The South Korean container ship PanStar Acro arrived in Busan on 11 October after a round trip along Russia's Northern Sea Route, the first use of the Arctic passage by a South Korean shipping company since 2016, Russian state news agency TASS reported, citing Yonhap. Lead with the voyage and the ten-year gap. The mechanism: say what the ship carried, between which ports and in how many days against the Suez route, whether it needed an icebreaker escort and Russian permits, and who chartered it, only as the page gives it. The structural point, stated carefully: the Arctic route runs through waters Russia controls and collects fees on, and a US ally's carrier has tested it while sanctions on Moscow are being argued over; draw no link to the Red Sea or Hormuz disruptions unless the page does. TASS is state media and the only source, relaying a South Korean agency: attribute to both, and treat any claim about the route's commercial promise as Moscow's. Dateline Busan.

stories.label: US: Justice Department probes Trump's press pool boycott
stories.summary: The US Justice Department's Antitrust Division says it is investigating five television networks over their joint decision to halt White House pool coverage of Donald Trump, with a spokeswoman saying 'group boycotts among commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act'. Lead with the probe and that sentence, quoted exactly. The mechanism: say what the pool is (the rotating crew the networks fund together to film the president), why the networks stopped and what they demanded, and how a law written against price-fixing cartels is being applied to an editorial decision; give the First Amendment answer media lawyers or the networks make, as the pages report it. The accountability point: the department that answers to the president is using competition law against the outlets that declined to broadcast him, weeks before the midterms. Say which networks, what the investigation can compel (documents, testimony) and what penalties the Sherman Act carries. Write from Deutsche Welle and Al Jazeera; Bloomberg may not fetch, and the Times of Israel item is a live-file entry. Write your own headline. Dateline Washington. US dateline (1 of 3).

stories.label: 2027: INEC excludes Pantami, Adebutu, clears Chinda in final governorship candidates' list
stories.summary: Nigeria's electoral commission, INEC, has published its final list of candidates for the 6 February 2027 governorship elections and left off prominent names, among them former minister Isa Pantami in Gombe and the PDP's Oladipupo Adebutu in Ogun, after a Supreme Court judgment restored a provision of the Electoral Act 2026 that limits party primaries to members on registers filed with INEC inside the statutory window. Lead with the exclusions and the rule that produced them. The mechanism: say what the provision requires, what the Supreme Court decided and when, how many candidates and which parties are affected, and what remedy an excluded candidate has before the vote. Then the dispute: the PDP in Ogun blames the ruling APC's 'desperation' (the second Premium Times item), and the NDC says its Kano candidate, Aminu Abdussalam Gwarzo, was dropped in error (BBC Hausa, in Hausa). The structural point: a membership-register rule, enforced by the referee four months out, decides who may be on the ballot before any voter does; state it without alleging intent the pages do not report. One clause: this follows Saturday's gunfire at an opposition rally in Enugu. Premium Times is the regional outlet. Write your own headline. Dateline Abuja.

stories.label: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella calls for AI 'emergency brake,' human control over advanced models- Moneycontrol.com
stories.summary: Microsoft's chief executive, Satya Nadella, has published an essay on X, 'Models as Insider Risks in the Super Intelligence Era', arguing that businesses should treat frontier AI models, closed and open-weight alike, as insider risks: like an employee with access who could do damage, and not because the model intends harm. Lead with that framing and with the 'emergency brake' he calls for, quoted exactly. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what controls he proposes (least-privilege access for agents, logging, a human able to halt a model, as the pages give them), what failure he has in mind (an agent with credentials acting on bad instructions or its own error), and how this differs from treating a model as a trusted tool. The accountability point: the warning comes from the company that sells these models into the enterprise through Copilot and Azure and holds a large stake in OpenAI, so say what Microsoft itself commits to and what it leaves to customers. This is an essay, not a product or a rule: state no capability as fact and report no policy that was not announced. Both sources are Indian outlets summarising the essay; quote only what they quote. Write your own headline. Dateline Redmond. US dateline (2 of 3).

stories.label: 请来Claude老祖，谷歌能借Agent翻身吗？
stories.summary: TMTPost, a mainland Chinese business outlet, reports on Google's bid to recover ground in AI agents, a contest over who supplies the base layer that agents run on, in which, the outlet says, OpenAI is again the target; the headline says Google has 'brought in' a figure or technology it calls the forefather of Claude. The feed carries only the headline and one line, so read the page first and lead with the concrete event it reports: who or what Google brought in, what was launched or announced, and when. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what the 'agent base layer' is (the model, the tool protocol and the runtime agents are built on), what Google is offering against OpenAI and Anthropic, and what the outlet thinks decides the contest. Distinct from the 10-10 piece on the Gemini 4 'Carbon' leak (one clause at most). This is a Chinese analysis piece on US companies: attribute every judgement to TMTPost, state no capability or hire as fact beyond what it documents, and say where its information comes from. In Chinese. Single source. Write your own headline. Dateline Mountain View, or Beijing if the piece is the outlet's own analysis; if Mountain View, a US dateline (3 of 3).

stories.label: Zimbabwe's dinosaurs were different from South Africa's: New species offers clues
stories.summary: Palaeontologists have described a new dinosaur species from Zimbabwe, and it differs from the animals known from South Africa's far better studied rocks of the same age, Phys.org reports. Lead with the species: its name, what kind of dinosaur it was, how old and how large, and where it was found. The mechanism for a technical reader: say what bones were recovered and which features set it apart, what the difference between the Zimbabwean and South African faunas implies (separate ecosystems or barriers across southern Africa at the time, as the researchers argue it), and how the age of the rock was established. Why it matters: most of what is known of early dinosaurs in Africa comes from a few South African basins, and a different fauna a few hundred kilometres north shows how much of the continent's record is unsampled; say who led the work and which Zimbabwean institutions and collectors took part, and where the fossil is kept. Name the journal and state the limits: how complete the specimen is. The feed entry was a teaser: write only what the page supports. Single source. Dateline Harare, or the city of the lead institution as the report gives it.

stories.label: Episodic isolation of the Arctic Mediterranean from the North Atlantic during late Pleistocene glacials
stories.summary: During some of the last ice ages the Arctic Ocean and Nordic Seas were at times cut off from the North Atlantic, a study in Communications Earth & Environment (a Nature Portfolio journal, not Nature itself: say so) concludes from sediment cores across the three basins. Lead with the finding in plain words: the sea that today exchanges water freely with the Atlantic was episodically isolated from it. The mechanism for a technical reader: the authors track the ratio of beryllium-10, made in the atmosphere by cosmic rays, to beryllium-9, washed in from land, and pair it with intervals of low thorium-230 excess; say what each tracer records and why together they point to a basin closed off, by ice shelves or lowered sea level as the paper argues, and say whether it supports the earlier proposal that the glacial Arctic filled with fresh water. Why it matters: Atlantic water flowing north is what keeps the Arctic's ice and Europe's climate as they are, and the record shows that exchange can stop. Name the lead author and institution, and state the limits: how many cores, how well dated, and what remains contested. Single source, the paper itself. Dateline the city of the lead institution.
